question: Which cell organelles are known as the cell's post office?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Golgi apparatus.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Golgi apparatus** is known as the** cell's post office** because it packages and distributes** molecules** (proteins and lipids) to different parts of the cell and outside the cell.
 
• It **modifies, sorts, and packages** the molecules in **vesicles** and sends them to their intended destinations.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is composed of stacks of flattened membranous sacs called** cisternae,** which are responsible for carrying out the aforementioned functions.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is present in **eukaryotic cells**, which include animal and plant cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The nucleus** is known as the control center of the cell, as it contains** genetic material (DNA).**

 
 
• It is responsible for regulating **cell growth, division, and metabolism.**
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes **are responsible for synthesizing proteins in the cell,
 
 
• They are either free in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
 
 
• **Plastids** are organelles found only in** plant cells** and are responsible for functions such as** photosynthesis, storage, and pigment synthesis**.
 
 
• Plastids include** chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and leucoplasts.**
